title: Introduce 'Thrifty' inference profile generator for conservative batching/caching/quant presets
author: Maya Chen
description: Adds a new service+CLI to synthesize conservative, production-safe default inference profiles from short trace samples. Motivation: many customers hesitate to enable aggressive batching/quantization/caching because they lack templates that balance unit-economics wins with latency/regression risk. This change introduces 'thrifty' profiles that err on the side of lower cost while preserving tail-latency SLOs. Key pieces: 1) trace-sampler: lightweight offline analyzer that ingests representative request traces and outputs distribution summaries (seq len, token mix, prefix reuse). 2) profile-generator: rules engine that maps trace summaries to a prioritized preset (batch size, prefetch window, prefix cache policy, int8/4 quantization candidate with safety fences). 3) rw-profile-gen CLI and Docker image for customers to run locally or in infra pipelines. 4) integration with recommendations API so Console can surface the generated profile and a one-click apply to dedicated/private deployments. The generator targets conservative defaults (microbatching on high-latency tails, small prefix caches for low-reuse workloads, disabled quant for short sequences) and emits an explainable rationale for each knob. Includes unit tests, e2e smoketest in the perf-canary harness, and docs for operators. This PR intentionally avoids aggressive heuristics (no automatic live rollouts) — it emits profiles as suggestions and supports a manual canary apply flow. Related: ENG-10233 (profile UX), SUP-3281 (customer support case triggered by runaway token costs).
